title: Honest Intervals for Survival Policy Values under Censoring and Unknown Decay
banked_reason: The proposed all-supplied-countable-space honest-adaptation characterization and a uniformly attaining interval remain open for finite |S|>=2 and H>2; the current core delivers boundary cases and a computable bracket instead of the promised whole-game theorem.
gap_reasons: The proposed all-supplied-countable-space honest-adaptation characterization and a uniformly attaining interval remain open for finite |S|>=2 and H>2; the current core delivers boundary cases and a computable bracket instead of the promised whole-game theorem.
proof_attempt_summary: Attempted a uniform all-countable-state original-record oracle and honest-adaptation characterization. The universal denominator fails for singleton spaces; discovery proved infinite-state, singleton, and two-transition boundary results but left finite state spaces of size at least two and horizons beyond two unresolved. The D0.5 rubric and two independent consults classified this replacement of the mandatory kernel by boundary cases and an open question as kernel substitution; no formalization was launched.
tldr: Honest precision for a frozen survival policy depends on what the original censored episodes reveal about late continuation. A surviving next-state indicator supplies an observable certificate for truncation bias. This yields a parent-honest prefix interval and the geometric-sum oracle frontier on infinite active spaces. A singleton active space instead permits root-\(n\) precision at every horizon, so the benchmark cannot be asserted for every supplied countable space. The central open question is the correctly indexed oracle frontier and exact price of unknown-decay adaptation across the remaining finite-state information geometries.
gap: Adaptive estimator comparisons do not automatically produce observable honest radii. Absorbing-MDP risk bounds and survival-value consistency do not characterize all honest intervals using partial transition records. The supplied benchmark additionally overlooks finite-state pooling.
fill: The theorem program retains the audited prefix and multilevel-hazard architecture, distinguishes infinite and singleton oracle denominators, and asks for matching honest-adaptation bounds in the original supplied-state-space experiment.
